newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes get boost from strong gas oil.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes get boost from strong gas oil.

text.p: The North Sea crude market was firm on Friday as outright values for benchmark Brent tracked futures higher, and a strong European gas oil market bolstered differentials for distillate-rich grades.
Traders pegged values for Dated Brent at Oct Brent parity to -5 cents, despite a sale late on Thursday of a 13-15 loader at Oct -10 cents.
"That was a distressed cargo," said the seller, "the later loaders aren't talking those kind of levels."
Cfds for next week were assessed at Oct Brent evens, while Sep 16-20 traded at Oct Brent -6 cents.
Oct Brent was talked around IPE screen levels which was trading up 22 cents at $22.38 a barrel by 1531 GMT.
Traders said that the North Sea market's relative buoyancy, despite perceptions of a prompt physical Brent overhang, was partly due to the strength of gas oil futures and physical markets.
"A lot of it has to do with the gas oil squeeze," said one major North Sea producer. "The gas oil-rich grades are benefitting."
The trader said that gas oil demand was behind the flurry of deals on North Sea grades on Thursday, particularly Forties.
A Statfjord cargo, loading 24-26, traded at a strong Dated Brent +30, against the last deal on Wednesday at Dated Brent +14 cents.
The transatlantic arbitrage was not viable, dealers said.
"The arb got crunched even more last night," said one dealer. "It could open if Dated falls further below October, but that doesn't look likely."
At least five Brent dates waiting to turn wet today were still on the move ahead of the five o'clock deadline, traders said.
